chunks: ...regarding the rats, and the cats, and the chickens, and the birds, and the dogs (falling into the well). He (peace be upon him) said: 'As long as they have not decomposed, or the taste of the water has not changed, then removing five buckets suffices you; and if the water has changed, then keep taking from it until the smell goes away.'

key_terms.الرِّيح: Literally 'wind/air', but here used for 'smell/odor' — the changed odor of the water
key_terms.دِلَاء: Plural of dalw (bucket/pail) — the vessel used to draw water from a well
key_terms.يَتَفَسَّخ: To decompose, putrefy, or disintegrate — referring to the animal carcass breaking apart

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an animal falls into a well according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a jurisprudential ruling on purifying a well into which various animals have fallen. If the animal has not decomposed and the water has not changed in taste, removing five buckets is sufficient for purification. However, if the water's taste or smell has been affected, one must keep drawing water until the odor completely dissipates. This ruling was addressed to Muslims of Medina and Kufa who relied on wells as their primary water source, for whom maintaining the purity of well water was a daily practical concern.
